note: Rests on item 0: Q3 is the first quantified look at the unquantified claims-lag/SNF cost problem against a $20-30m EBITDA guide, on a name whose last three prints fell 20/10/6 and whose beats are sold; shrunk hard because the direction is already half-priced (-16% on Sept 15, PTs halved) and items 1 and 4 (benign peer MA trend, 2027 growth with competitors exiting) cut the other way.

Item 0 is the best thing on the day: arithmetic straight off the company's own releases shows H2 needs +16.2% while management guided case volume and price DOWN and EOS needs ~+48% half-on-half after two cuts, with FY consensus pinned at $882.06m (range $881.8-882.6m) so no trim is modelled — and this name's guidance-line surprises printed -31.7% and -22.3%; netted against the CEO's first open-market buy (item 1), which is a real counterweight on the quarter but not on the FY guide.

Two-sided and large: the permit-exclusive guide as a floor with consensus parked on it (item 0) plus a Chinese-language peer print showing InP volume AND price up (item 1) and a capacity raise that backlog corroborates (item 2), against a Q4 consensus of $77.45m sitting above the stated ~$60m/quarter capacity ceiling (item 3); sized only modestly positive because the -14.6 skew already pays for upside, so the long side is partly priced while the Q4-guide risk is not.

Near a wash: the one document-backed mechanism is item 6 (Baillie Gifford's 5.4% stake to zero by 9/30 with Pale Fire absorbing 2.3m shares at $4.6-5.1, i.e. the seller that drove the slide to the low is finished) plus a 10.7%-of-float short at the 52-week low with calls bid, set against item 2, the enterprise NRR slide to 91% and the Q4/2027 dis-synergy framing, which is precisely the line that produced -14.7%, -11.6% and -12.9% on the last three prints; the beat case (items 0-1) is real but this name sells its beats.

Small and negative: every item here is public and read by the whole street on the most-covered name in the universe, so the only thing with teeth is item 4 — the bar sits above Intel's own guide after seven straight guidance beats, the stock is up ~150% YTD, and the last two beat-and-raises printed -7.9% and -8.5% — reinforced by item 3's asymmetry, where a call silent on 14A names undercuts a story the market has already been handed; the server-supply (item 0) and 18A margin (item 6) positives are three months old and in the price.
